newsitem.title: UK: Halifax boosted by instituional demand.
newsitem.headline: Halifax boosted by instituional demand.

text.p: Shares in Britain's biggest mortgage lender, Halifax Plc, opened strongly on their first day of trading on Monday as demand among institutions gave an initial boost to the stock.
The shares opened at 774-1/2 pence each, valuing the group at around 19.4 billion pounds, before the shares slipped back to stand at 756 pence by the end of the first hour of trading.
A shortage of stock among financial institutions and pension funds lifted the shares well above fundamental valuations, put by many analysts at between 580 pence and 650 pence.

"Our analysis suggests that 600-650 pence is about where it should be based on its fundamental prospects vis a vis the other shares in the UK financial sector," said Salomon banking analyst John Leonard who rates the stock a hold.
"Halifax may be a great company but it's a rich share."
